strengths: Best-in-pair metric semantics: attempt events vs affected orders, a stated resolved denominator with exclusion counts, pp vs count deltas and no invented target/cause (analysis.md:20-27; desktop.png).
Clear investigation flow with a quantified non-causal headline, context chips on the orders view, inline details and preserved filters (analysis.md:43-117).
Honest charting with exact alternatives: 0-100% rate axis with dashed comparison, hatched comparison bars, data table and keyboard day targets (analysis.md:74-90; app.js:688-850).
A complete state taxonomy, including in-progress, stale, partial, error/retry, no-data, empty result and no-denominator (analysis.md:119-135).
The page does not horizontally overflow at 390 px (checks.json:69-71), and the mobile cards stack readably.

comparison: Candidate A has the stronger desktop information architecture and investigation model: a context strip, computed insight, KPI -> trend/mix -> regional table -> drawer sequence, with preserved filters and focus. Candidate B has the stronger product/metric semantics (attempt events vs orders, explicit denominator and exclusions) and the cleaner 390 px page. Both deliver a broken viewport: Candidate A overflows horizontally at 390 px with a 604 px document, while Candidate B's cards fall out of the 12-column grid because of a stray closing tag, producing a blank right column. Candidate A's accessibility violations are more numerous (22 contrast nodes), but its state and interaction coverage is at least as complete; Candidate B's table-sort copy is not delivered. Candidate A edges ahead on hierarchy, design reasoning and completeness; Candidate B is better on domain modeling and responsive integrity.
limitations: Only normal-state screenshots are supplied for both candidates; loading, stale, partial, no-data, error, empty and drawer/orders states were assessed from source and prose, not rendered evidence. checks.json is an axe-based rendered summary, not a full functional or WCAG test, and Candidate B's claimed 77/77 and 13/13 checks are absent from the packet. Candidate A's mobile image is 604 px wide at a 390 px viewport, so 390 px visual judgement is partly inferred from the reported overflow and DOM. No screen-reader, cross-browser or real-data testing was available. This is one blinded judge pass, not a statistical test or proof of causation.
